inputs.share_count_basis: 691,811,346 issued less 4,390,787 treasury (incl. ~0.8m BIP Trust shares) at 2026-06-30 = 687.42m; no convertibles or options outstanding, so basic = fully diluted. Held FLAT: buybacks (JPY58.1bn FY2026, JPY12.2bn FY2025) are value-neutral in this model and are not credited as a shrinking count.
inputs.sbc_source: J-GAAP filer with no share-based-compensation add-back in the cash flow statement. The only equity-settled pay is the directors' BIP Trust (provision for share awards JPY703m balance, ~0.8m trust shares); immaterial and already inside SG&A. Treated as an SBC-zero market: SBC rows kept explicit at 0%.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-26T01:27:40Z (Tokyo regular session; Yahoo Finance chart API)
inputs.net_debt_note: Q1 FY2027 tanshin (balance sheet at 2026-06-30): cash and deposits 457,543 vs interest-bearing debt 342,856 (short-term borrowings 78,405 + current nonrecourse 9,321 + current bonds 20,066 + bonds 40,009 + long-term borrowings 140,693 + nonrecourse loans 54,362). Nonrecourse real-estate loans are included in debt. Current 'Securities' of 9,687 are left out of cash (conservative). Lease liabilities (3,058 + 9,748 = 12,806) are excluded -- see lease_treatment. Net cash of JPY114.7bn is ~0.9x the owner-FCF base, so FY2026 interest income (5,234) is stripped from the flows and the cash sits in the bridge instead.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in JPY, the currency of the flows. Cost of equity 7.7% = 10y JGB ~1.7% (Oct 2026) + beta 1.0 x Japan ERP 6.0%. Debt ~14% of market-value capital at ~1.0% after tax. Mechanical WACC ~6.8%; rounded up to 7.5% because a thin-moat, fixed-price-contract general contractor carries project and claim risk that a market beta understates. Cyclicality and margin mean-reversion are charged in the FLOWS (base-case margin normalised below FY2026, bear-case trough) -- the same 7.5% is used in all three scenarios so risk is not charged twice.
inputs.lease_treatment: (B) leases as operating cost. J-GAAP: operating leases are expensed inside cost of sales / SG&A, so no lease add-back inflates EBITDA; finance-lease liabilities (JPY12.8bn) are excluded from net debt and the small lease principal repayment (JPY2.9bn FY2026) is covered by the capex line. No separate lease_cost_pct_path is needed.
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are consolidated (EBITDA-based). Non-controlling interests (JPY55,305m at 2026-06-30; NCI took JPY4.0bn of JPY177.8bn FY2026 profit, ~2.3%) are deducted ONCE in the equity bridge. FY0 check: FY2026 operating profit 194,678 x (1-0.31) = 134.3bn NOPAT vs attributable net income 173.8bn -- the gap is the JPY49.0bn extraordinary gain on cross-shareholding sales plus 12.1bn interest/dividend income, both of which are excluded from the flows and represented by the securities/cash lines in the bridge.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (dcf-methods routing: non-US cyclical operating company; owner-fcf.md + owner-fcf-adaptations.md read in full). Obayashi is a Big-4 Japanese general contractor; a going-concern FCF model is the right frame. KEY JUDGMENT -- MARGIN NORMALISATION: FY2026 operating margin of 7.5% (op profit 194.7bn) is treated as a cyclical high, not a run-rate. Management's own FY2027 guidance is op profit 180.0bn on sales 2,945bn (6.1%), citing fewer projects in the final, most-profitable completion stage and non-repeat of claim approvals and property-sale gains. Ten-year operating margin history: FY2017-21 7.0-7.6%, FY2022-24 trough 2.1-4.7% (cost inflation on pre-inflation fixed-price backlog), FY2025 5.5%, FY2026 7.5%; 10-yr mean 5.95%. Base case follows guidance to 6.1% in FY2027 then settles at ~5.75% EBIT (7.25% EBITDA less 1.5% D&A) -- a mid-cycle margin, with the rising overseas mix (2-4% segment margins, now ~35% of sales) offsetting better domestic pricing. FY0 OWNER FCF: reported FCF 127,290 (OCF 252,920 less capex 125,630) less interest income 5,234 = 122,056. This FY0 figure is NOT carried forward: FY2026 OCF was flattered by a JPY106.5bn rise in advances received, and FY2026 capex (4.9% of sales) was a peak year of the Medium-Term Plan's JPY845bn investment programme (real estate development, GCON, machinery, DX). The component build gives year-1 owner FCF of ~JPY63bn (2.2% of sales), in line with the FY2017-26 average reported FCF of ~JPY60bn/yr -- Japanese contractors convert earnings to FCF poorly because they recycle profit into leasing real estate. CAPEX: 3.5% of sales in FY2027-28 (MiTASUN data-centre venture ~JPY100bn through FY2028, real estate pipeline), easing to 3.0%; D&A 1.45-1.5%. CASH TAX: 31% (Japan statutory ~30.6%; FY2026 cash tax paid 82.2bn was inflated by tax on securities gains). WORKING CAPITAL: net contract working capital is roughly neutral (receivables + WIP ~1.19tn vs payables + advances + deposits ~1.13tn at June 2026), so base capture 0%; bear -5% of revenue change as overseas receivables stretch. EQUITY BRIDGE (matching-asset rule): dividend income (6.8bn) and the recurring extraordinary gains on cross-shareholding sales (49.0bn FY2026, 68.7bn FY2025) are OUTSIDE operating profit, so the investment-securities portfolio enters the bridge at fair value net of deferred tax instead; NCI and the unfunded pension are deducted. MULTIPLEX: the ~US$650m (~JPY95-100bn incl. earn-out) acquisition of Multiplex Global from Brookfield, announced 2026-06-18 and expected to close ~Q4 CY2026, is NOT in the 2026-06-30 balance sheet and its flows are NOT in the projections (FY2027 guidance predates it). It is treated as NPV-neutral -- cash paid equals business value received -- which is the honest default for a ~1-2% margin contractor bought at a market price; integration risk is in the bear case. HOUSE = STREET: with SBC at zero the two bases coincide and band_position is null. HURDLE: house 15% kept for comparability; for JPY flows at a 1.7% risk-free rate it is a demanding bar and the required-return table is the better guide. The 10-year horizon is used although the margin matures by year 4, so the entry price and required-return table are on the house N=10 convention.

equity_bridge.item: Investment securities (cross-shareholdings) at fair value, net of deferred tax on unrealised gains

Dividend income and sale gains are outside the modelled flows (matching-asset rule). Company is selling down to <20% of net assets by March 2027.

equity_bridge.note: Retirement benefit liability 50,564 less retirement benefit asset 13,688 (March 2026 figure) = 36,876 x (1-0.306).

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: equity_5yr_cagr (6.2%) tempered to the base-path 10-year revenue CAGR (~3.5%): FY2027 guided +13.9% is backlog conversion, after which domestic volume is capacity-constrained by labour and growth is price-led
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 6.2% vs EPS 5yr CAGR 12.6% diverge by >30%: the EPS series runs from the FY2021 margin peak through the FY2022 trough (EPS 54.55) back to a new peak, so point-to-point EPS CAGRs are cycle artefacts. Owner-FCF CAGRs: 3yr -2.3% (FY2023 130.7bn -> FY2026 122.1bn); 5yr undefined because FY2021 owner FCF was negative (-33.5bn). Reported FCF over FY2017-26 averaged ~60bn/yr with four negative or near-zero years -- FCF is lumpy with advances/receivables timing and should not be trended.

base.growth_rationale: Y1 = FY2027 guidance (sales 2,945bn, +13.9%, reaffirmed Aug 2026; Q1 +19%). FY2027 orders guided 3,100bn (book-to-bill 1.05) supports FY2028 +4%. Thereafter domestic volume is capped by the shrinking skilled workforce, so growth is largely price/mix: 2-3% fading to 1.5%.
base.margin_rationale: Y1 EBITDA 7.55% = guided op margin 6.1% + D&A 1.45% (op profit ties to the 180bn guide). Then settles at 7.25% EBITDA / 5.75% EBIT -- the FY2017-26 mean op margin is 5.95% and overseas mix (2-4% margins) is rising. FY2026's 7.5% (domestic building 9.1%) is treated as peak-of-cycle.
base.capex_rationale: 3.5% of sales FY2027-28 (data-centre venture, real estate pipeline, machinery; MTBP investing outflow ~JPY84bn/yr avg) easing to 3.0%; D&A 1.5%. Net investment ~1.5% of sales sustains the real-estate book that earns the ~20bn real-estate segment profit inside EBITDA.
base.terminal_rationale: g = 1.0% nominal JPY for a mature, labour-constrained domestic market. Cap 14x terminal FCF (cyclical, thin moat); the cap binds in base at WACC 7.5% / g 1.0% (Gordon 15.5x).

bull.narrative: Management's FY2027 guide proves conservative (as Q1's +107% op profit hints), domestic building holds 8-9% margins on disciplined bidding, overseas margins lift to 4-5% as GCON data-centre/semiconductor work scales, and the 7% op margin becomes the new normal (8.5% EBITDA). Growth stays mid-single-digit on the data-centre and urban-redevelopment cycle; capex normalises to 2.8% once MiTASUN is built.

bear.narrative: FY2027 backlog still converts (+12%) but at a 5.35% op margin as claim approvals dry up; then a renewed cost-inflation squeeze on fixed-price backlog (the FY2022-24 pattern) takes the op margin to ~4% while orders fall after the large-project cohort (FY2026 orders already -9.9%) and labour caps capacity, so revenue shrinks for two years. GCON/Multiplex integration absorbs management and cash; overseas receivables stretch (WC -5% of revenue change). Op margin recovers only to ~4.5% (6.0% EBITDA). Terminal cap 12x.

scenario_narratives.base: FY2027 follows management's guide: sales +13.9% to 2,945bn on backlog conversion, op profit down 7.5% to 180bn (6.1%) as fewer projects sit in their final, most-profitable stage and FY2026's claim approvals and property-sale gains do not repeat. From FY2028 the business is a mature, labour-constrained Big-4 contractor growing 1.5-4% with a mid-cycle 5.75% EBIT margin -- below FY2026's 7.5% peak but above the FY2017-26 mean -- reinvesting ~1.5% of sales net into real estate and data centres. Value is roughly half operating flows, a quarter terminal and a quarter balance sheet (net cash plus cross-shareholdings).
scenario_narratives.bull: The margin step-up is structural, not cyclical: inflation-indexed contracts, oligopoly discipline on mega-projects and data-centre/semiconductor specialisation (GCON, MiTASUN) hold the group op margin near 7%, overseas margins rise, and growth stays 3-6% through the decade. Capex eases as the MTBP investment wave passes.
scenario_narratives.bear: The 2022-24 playbook repeats: cost inflation and the labour shortage squeeze fixed-price backlog, op margin falls to ~4%, orders roll over after the large-project cohort and revenue contracts for two years; Multiplex/GCON integration disappoints and working capital absorbs cash on overseas projects. Margins recover only to ~4.5%, and the market caps the business at 12x FCF.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 30%: this is a thin-moat cyclical valued off a margin management itself says is coming down, the labour constraint is structural, and the FY2022-24 trough shows how fast a 7% margin becomes 2%. Bull cut to 20%: it needs three independent things -- domestic margins holding at peak, overseas margins doubling, and growth staying mid-single-digit despite capacity limits -- plus a clean integration of two cross-border acquisitions. Base 50%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A general contractor is valued on mid-cycle owner FCF, not on peak-year earnings. FY2026's 7.5% operating margin and 14.4% ROE are the top of a cycle that management has already guided down; the base case normalises the EBIT margin to 5.75% and converts earnings to cash at the historical ~2.5% of sales after the real-estate and data-centre reinvestment the company has committed to. The balance sheet (net cash plus a JPY300bn cross-shareholding book being sold down) is worth ~JPY500/share and is counted once, in the bridge, with the income it produces excluded from the flows. Multiplex is treated as NPV-neutral until its first consolidated results.
key_risks_to_valuation: Margin normalisation judgment: if 7%+ op margins prove structural (bull), base IV is understated by roughly a third; if the FY2022-24 cost squeeze recurs (bear), it is overstated by a similar amount

FCF conversion: the model assumes ~1.5% of sales of net reinvestment forever; if the real-estate/data-centre programme ends and capex falls to D&A, FCF margin rises by ~1.5pp of sales (~+JPY700/share)
Cross-shareholding value (JPY247bn after tax, ~JPY360/share) depends on equity-market levels; the company is a forced seller down to 20% of net assets by March 2027
Multiplex (~JPY95-100bn) and GCON integration: a loss-making overseas project book is the classic way a Japanese contractor destroys a decade of domestic profit
Working-capital timing: advances received rose JPY106bn in FY2026 and can reverse; a single year's FCF says little
Compliance tail risk: 2018 maglev bid-rigging conviction; renewed antitrust action on mega-project tenders
WACC: at 7.5% in JPY the valuation is terminal-light (cap binds) but still sensitive -- each 1pp of WACC moves base IV by roughly JPY250-300/share
